Prologue.Title: The Footfall Oath
Prologue.Crawl:
Every child in the town learns the same three things before they learn their letters. The ground below is not your friend. The Longmother does not stop. And when she puts a foot down, somebody has to go and stand where it landed.

That somebody is the vanguard. Crews of a handful, sworn at the rail with a hand on her warm plate, lowered on chains into the dust of each new footfall to clear whatever her step woke before the caravan's wheels roll down after it. Most crews last a season. The good ones last two. Nobody's lasted long enough to say what's past the edge of the old maps.

The last crew that held the forward chains didn't come back up from the Green Valley drop. The rail is empty, the bell is ringing, and the council has run out of veterans to ask.

So they're asking you.

You've never cleared a footfall. You've never seen what the blight makes of a living thing that held still too long. You don't know yet that every crew who ever swore this oath swore it for a different reason -- coin, debt, faith, a name to clear, someone below they couldn't leave.

You'll learn all of that on the road. For now there's only the oath, the chain, and the ground coming up fast.

Drop at the footfall. Clear what the step disturbed. Be back on the chain before she walks on.

Ending.Title: The Longmother Walks On
Ending.Crawl:
The Vampire Lord falls the way everything on this road was always meant to: all at once, after holding still far too long.

There is no cure in his ashes. The wells of Veshker stay sour, the stone keeps its rot, and somewhere under the world the blight goes on doing what it has always done, patient as the ground itself. That was never the fight you could win.

The fight you could win was simpler. A ruler who couldn't bear to keep walking had reached up from his dead city to drag the Longmother down beside him -- to make the last moving thing on this road stand still and spoil like everything else. He didn't get her. She felt the knot go out of the road the way a sleeper feels a stone leave her shoe, and she walked on without breaking stride.

The bell at the rail rings once, for the crew that came back up the chain. Not veterans anymore. Not strangers, either -- whatever each of you swore for at the start, you found something the oath didn't mention: each other, and the plain stubborn work of keeping a whole town moving one footfall at a time.

She curls the road ahead toward green country again, deeper than any map has ever run. The blight is older there. Whatever has been growing in that ground has had longer, undisturbed, to get good at it.

The chains are already being oiled.

The road continues.

Themes.Name: Green Valley
Themes.Crawl:
The town is the Longmother's back. Nobody alive remembers her hatching, and nobody can say how long the streets above her have been nailed down to old carapace plate -- only that she has never once stood still long enough for anyone to ask. Standing ground goes bad. Somewhere under the world a blight is souring the earth, and it only ever catches up with what holds still.

Green Valley is the last green ground on the old road, and it's already going: the wells have a taste to them, and the frogs that used to keep to the marsh edge are coming up onto dry land in numbers nobody's seen. This isn't an attack. It's the first proof that staying was never actually safe here -- it just hadn't caught up yet.

Every footfall breaks ground that's been undisturbed, sometimes for centuries, and whatever's been growing down there -- part rot, part something stranger, metal fused to bone that shouldn't move and does -- comes up through the crack before the town's even finished passing overhead. That's the vanguard crews' work: drop at the footfall, clear what the step disturbed, salvage what it turned up, before she walks on. Gear grown from her own molted plate, not mined; the pincer copied from watching her brood hunt; every action taken on her clock, not yours.

Lately the orbs flicker and the wards don't always catch where the ground's worst -- nobody's cast a clean spell within a day's walk of a bad well in a month. That's why the caravan is leaning harder on what can be built and burned than on what has to be summoned. It isn't superstition. It's logistics.

Themes.Name: Sandsea Reaches
Themes.Crawl:
Sandsea Reaches is country the Longmother has crossed before, maybe more than once -- wagon ruts run under the dunes that aren't hers, old and half-swallowed. The sand keeps what it takes: goblin clans who dug in here generations back are still down there, and her footfalls are turning their old works back up into daylight, diggers and all.

The heat and the thirst are the obvious danger. The quieter one is what the crew pulls out of the ground between skirmishes -- the first clean proof that the blight isn't just rot with a smell. It has a shape now: joints that shouldn't bend, plating that grew instead of being forged, creatures half built and half born that were neither, a season ago.

Spellcraft frays worse out here than it did in the valley -- a caster's orb can gutter mid-word in exactly the stretch of sand where the ground is sickest, as if the blight and the old magic can't stand to share the same air. The Alchemist's brews don't care what the air is doing. That's the whole of her argument for coming along.

Themes.Name: Mireholt Fens
Themes.Crawl:
Mireholt Fens is wet, low ground, and the blight doesn't dry out and blow off here the way it does elsewhere -- it pools, the way water does, which is why so much trouble sits in so small a stretch of road. Hags and swamp-things aren't passing through; they've made a rotting home of exactly the low ground the Longmother has to cross, and they are not glad to have her overhead.

This is the leg of the route where the crew can finally say it out loud: the work is getting harder faster than the road is getting easier. Every fen is worse than the last fen.

It's also where the lights first answered the dark -- someone out here already knew how to bind a working tight enough to survive the interference the wetter ground throws at it, rather than cast one loose and hope. Runes sewn into steel hold their shape where a spoken spell comes apart. The caravan needed that, whether or not it knew it yet.

Themes.Name: Frostmaw Caverns
Themes.Crawl:
The road climbs out of the fens into Frostmaw, and for once the danger underfoot isn't what the Longmother's own feet stirred up -- it's what was already waiting, down where the mineral veins run that have fed the caravan's mana casks since before anyone currently walking remembers tapping them.

Cold keeps things slow, the blight included, which means whatever's down here has had the one thing nothing else on the route has had: time to grow old, untouched, instead of being swept along with everything else the footfalls disturb.

Here the crew finds the first thing that was unmistakably built, not merely grown or buried -- machined edges, a purpose to the shape of it that no animal or ruin accounts for. That's the turning point. Whatever is wearing the blight this far along the road didn't just happen to it. Something made it this way, on purpose, a long time before the Longmother ever walked this close.

Themes.Name: Veshker Ruins
Themes.Crawl:
Veshker Ruins is a dead city -- stone instead of carapace, built by people who tried to do what the town does without ever learning to walk. They dug in, raised walls, and told themselves that walls built well enough were the same as never standing still. They failed the way every grounded thing on this road eventually fails.

Except here, something never let the failure finish. The Vampire Lord was the city's ruler once, and when the blight came for him the way it comes for everything that stops, he found a way to keep "stopped" going long after it should have killed him. He isn't trying to outrun the blight anymore. He's past that. He wants the Longmother to stop, too -- so that he can finally be still on ground that won't rot out from under him.

This is the climax of the road so far: not another step ahead of something chasing, but a straight refusal to make the mistake this whole city already made.

Themes.Name: Green Valley, Deeper In
Themes.Crawl:
The Vampire Lord's fall didn't end the march, and it didn't cure anything -- the blight doesn't go anywhere just because its best host finally did. It only cleared one knot out of the road ahead.

The Longmother can't double back the way she came; ground she's already woken stays bad long after she's past it, so her route has never been a straight line so much as a long curl, carrying her back, again and again, through the same kinds of country rather than the same ground. This is that curl closing on green country again -- deeper than the old road ever ran, country the valley's own maps never reached.

It looks like home. It isn't. The wells here never had travelers to warn them, and whatever's been working on this ground has had longer, undisturbed, to get good at it.

Themes.Name: Sandsea Reaches, Further Out
Themes.Crawl:
Further out than the Reaches the crew already crossed, the dunes keep going, and so does the blight's handiwork -- what was a rare, unsettling find back at the oasis is common country out here. Half-grown, half-built things aren't the exception on this stretch of sand. They're what's expected.

It's the clearest evidence yet that whatever wears the blight well enough -- tagged, in the caravan's own blunt shorthand, a Demon Lord, as if it were one title and not a condition -- isn't one throne the crew is marching toward. It's a shape the blight keeps finding again, out here, wherever the host is strong enough to hold it.

Themes.Name: Mireholt Fens, Past the Mire
Themes.Crawl:
Past the mire the crew already fought through, the fen only gets wetter, and the blight that pools here has had longer to settle than anywhere else on the route. The crew isn't the only vanguard working this ground, either -- wreckage further in carries markings that aren't the caravan's, and the people who left it are either still down here or didn't get the chance to leave.

Whoever they were, they weren't chasing glory. Out past the mire, nobody comes this far who still has somewhere better to be.

Themes.Name: Frostmaw Caverns, Lower Depths
Themes.Crawl:
Lower than the veins the caravan has mined for a generation, the caves keep going, following the same seams down toward wherever the thing the crew found earlier -- built, not grown, not buried by accident -- was built. The mana ore gets thinner and stranger the deeper the crew follows it, half-crystal and half-something-else, and less and less of it burns clean.

It's the sharpest the choice has ever felt: spend what little reliable fuel the depths still give up, or trust a casting in ground this far gone. Most of the crew doesn't trust it anymore.

Themes.Name: Veshker Ruins, Inner Wards
Themes.Crawl:
Past the wards the Vampire Lord held, deeper into Veshker than the fight that ended him ever reached, the ruins keep going -- older construction under the newer, and under that, older still. Whoever built the city's failed foundations wasn't the first to try keeping ground still here, either.

The road doesn't end at a dead king's throne. It just goes on being the only question the caravan has ever actually been chasing: not how to beat what's down here, but what, at the bottom of all of it, the blight actually is. Nobody in the crew has an answer yet. That's as far as the road has carried them so far.
